args.report: I utilized the structural analysis of $f(n) \pmod 4$ to find a simple, general construction for $u$ when $v=p$ is an odd prime. By requiring the first difference, $f(u+p) - f(u)$, to be $0 \pmod 4$, I determined that setting $u=4$ works if and only if $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. This construction yields $f(4+p) - f(4) = (4+p) - 1 = 3+p$, which is a multiple of 4 when $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. This pattern was verified for $p=5$.

I investigated even values of v > 4. I proved that a necessary structural condition for a solution u to exist for any even v is that v must be a multiple of 4. This is because for both even and odd u, the differences $f(u+v) - f(u)$ or $f(u+v+1) - f(u+1)$ simplify to v. Consequently, no solution exists for v=6. For the specific case v=8, which satisfies the necessary condition, I tested small values of u (u=6, u=1) and found counterexamples. For u=6, the condition fails for j=6 ($f(20)-f(12)=2$), and for u=1, the condition fails for j=3 ($f(12)-f(4)=2$), strongly indicating that solutions are highly unlikely to exist for v=8 either.
